cases.rationale: No invalidating or expiring event: each claim remains current.
Load-cell calibration expiry suspends bond strength only; WCA and aging claims use different calibration dependencies.
Aging-chamber calibration drift affects every dependent aging claim, not unrelated initial strength or wettability.
A process drift event invalidates only claims dependent on the affected process profile.
An event outside every claim dependency closure does not suspend this passport.
Confirmed withdrawal of the exact bond-test source revokes only claims that rely on it.
A suspected field failure suspends the related life claim pending review without declaring causation or revoking unrelated claims.
A confirmed review-due event expires only the claim whose review dependency is due.
A claim with an explicit review deadline expires when the evaluation time reaches the deadline.
A declared validity interval is not assumed to continue after its end.
A qualified successor explicitly supersedes its predecessor; historical generation remains represented with its prior state.
Exact replay of an immutable event ID and identical payload is idempotent.
Reusing one event ID with a different source digest is a contradiction, not a harmless duplicate.
A sequence gap or missing predecessor must not be silently reordered.
The first event cannot claim an absent predecessor.
The system cannot infer impact scope from an absent or malformed dependency-closure reference.
A future-effective event is recorded but does not invalidate a claim before its effective time.
An event interval wholly before the generation's effective period does not invalidate that generation.
A method receipt outside its registered material scope cannot underwrite a currently qualified claim.
An unrecognized test-method edition blocks admission until the controlled edition is reviewed.
An incomplete protocol receipt cannot support a current method-measurement claim.
A generation cannot claim an absent predecessor.
A supersession event requires an existing qualified successor generation.
An event cannot target a generation that is absent from the manifest.
Event effective time without a declared time source cannot establish affected exposure scope.
An event timestamp later than its ingestion timestamp is a known temporal contradiction.
An effective interval ending before it begins is invalid.
An explicit generation-targeted fault affects all claims within that passport generation.
